questions.text: Why does retrying a mutation with a new JSON-RPC request ID fail to prevent duplicate side effects?

options.A: Request IDs are automatically reused by every server instance.
options.B: A new request ID always invalidates the previous committed result.
options.C: Request IDs correlate messages; a durable application key must identify the business intent.
options.D: Only transport connection IDs can deduplicate business operations.

questions.explanation: JSON-RPC IDs match requests and responses. Business deduplication requires an application idempotency key bound to identical arguments and durably enforced.

questions.text: Progress arrives just before every idle timeout, but the operation keeps running. Which policy prevents an endless request?

options.A: Reset both idle and maximum deadlines on every progress event.
options.B: Remove the maximum deadline when a progress token exists.
options.C: Treat SSE keepalive comments as proof the operation is making progress.
options.D: Keep an absolute maximum deadline unaffected by progress.

questions.explanation: Progress may reset the idle clock but must not extend the absolute operation budget.

questions.text: RequestCoordinator.complete first returns None when request.state==CANCELLED. Cancellation is accepted before the worker calls complete(). What happens?

options.A: complete returns None and emits no final response for that cancelled request.
options.B: complete changes the state to COMPLETED and sends the result anyway.
options.C: complete raises a protocol error that must be sent to the client.
options.D: complete starts a new task so the result can be delivered later.

questions.explanation: The CANCELLED guard exits before constructing, storing, or emitting a response, so cancellation wins this event ordering.
